reviews.text:
This was my third visit since my first visit.
The menu changes every week, so I make reservations after looking at Instagram on Wednesdays. The pasta is new every time I go, and the conversation with the owner increases every time I go.
I think I'm now addicted to pasta that tastes like something I would eat at an Italian home rather than a sophisticated dish.
This beloved restaurant has become the first restaurant that comes to mind when you think of “pasta,” thanks to the generous taste of its ingredients and the cheerful owner.

(First visit)
My wife tried to make a reservation a few times but couldn't, so I was curious about what kind of place it was, but I succeeded in making a reservation and visited on Sunday lunch.
It is said to be open only on weekends, and the menu features two types of pasta that change weekly. It is located on the hill leading up to Naksan Mountain.

What was impressive was
1. I was surprised by the building that looked like a corner store in the past and the very narrow interior. The seat I was shown to was a large table shared by three teams, but the books and tables around it made me think it was a place where group tutoring used to be held.
2. It was octopus pasta in tomato sauce and pistachio cream pasta.
- The octopus pasta was the best as it had a soft texture and was not tough like the octopus tasted locally.
- The pistachio cream pasta was good because the non-greasy cream and savory pistachios went well with the rigatoni noodles, and there was plenty of thick bacon, so I could enjoy it with the noodles until the end.
3. The owner came during the meal and cut the bread himself. He said that he had studied abroad in Italy and that his sociability had improved a lot there, and he made me feel like he was a cheerful Taoist. He came back at the end of the meal and gave us a piece of octopus each, leaving a good impression on my wife, who is a Southern European octopus addict.

I enjoy eating pasta, so I thought I had some knowledge, but I think Osso's pasta has a uniqueness and taste that is hard to find in other Italian restaurants, and I think it's a restaurant comparable to the now-closed Tuto Bene. As soon as I returned, I had such a great experience that my wife and I were thinking about returning again, and I'm looking forward to the next time I try pasta and chatting with the owner.

It seems to be so well known that you can't eat there without a reservation, and since there aren't many tables, people who come without a reservation often turn away.
Spanish dishes are served with a slightly sweet Korean flavor, and the red interior color seems to add more flavor. The tapas taste good and it looks like it's homemade bread, so it's good to top it with dishes, but the amount of bread wasn't that much, so I had to order it multiple times.
Personally, I was generally satisfied with the dish, and although I felt it was a little stronger than the food I ate in Spain, it went well with the wine.

As for food, everything we ordered was delicious.
I highly recommend the honey cod and Porqueno style octopus dishes. There was lasagna, gambas al japkin, honey eggplant fries (this one was medium), and jamon. When you order jamon, you can see it being cut right in front of your eyes. It was a shame that I couldn't eat the pork belly because I ran out of ingredients.

reviews.text:
I had a cheeseburger set and chicken sticks (8 pieces).
The cheeseburger set is 8,700 won and the chicken stick is 2,000 won.
The burger set alone was very satisfying.
It's unusual that the burger has sesame seeds on the bottom. The bun was a bit soggy. It goes well with the patty juiciness, but it doesn't suit my taste, which likes the texture on the outside. It's better than McDonald's beef burger. The patties are thick as if they were baked at home. The advantage and disadvantage is that it is simple. People who like provocative things might find it a bit boring. The fries are the quintessential handmade burger fries. It's thick and light. I think it would taste better if I seasoned it a little bit. They only provide ketchup sauce, but I suggest that you also provide salt and pepper.
Chicken sticks were special. It had just the right amount of spiciness, and although it was a bit thin on the outside, it was still delicious in its own way.
The portion is generous. It's exactly the taste that comes to mind from the ingredients. The Spicy Hash Bacon Cheese Burger and Bacon Cheese Burger are both a bit salty. Last time, the regular cheeseburger wasn't salty, so I guess it was salty because of the bacon. The Spicy Hash Bacon Cheese Burger wasn't spicy at all and the hash was surprisingly sweet. reviews.text:
This is a handmade burger restaurant located in Daehakro.

The atmosphere of the store is that of a Hanok building, but the inside is a fairly new building. Actually, there are some things that feel like a bit of a mismatch. The volume of music inside is so loud that it feels a bit awkward to sit there for a long time.

I ordered the double beef mushroom cheese burger set (11,700 won). The burger here has a really killer patty. You can really taste the heavy, fatty meat. Be sure to order and try the double beef.

French fries are... sore fingers. French fries can't match the taste of a burger at all. It's poor and damp.  There used to be mayonnaise there, but mayonnaise is gone... If you're going to order a set, I'd say it's better to order it individually.

Unlimited refills are available for drinks. It's in the form of a dispenser that mixes syrup with carbonated water, and the taste changes every time you come. This point is also a minus.

But even taking all of this into account, the taste of the patty and burger really makes up for it all. I think it's worth a visit at least once when you visit Daehakro. I think this is a house that I can easily recommend to people around me.

I recommend it.

reviews.author: FNH
reviews.text:
“Authentic smoke barbecue in the middle of Seoul”

Smoke Train is a barbecue restaurant hidden deep in an alley in Jongno.
It is an American smoke house style restaurant with impressive smoky meat and deep flavor.

🔸Food quality

The quality of smoked meats such as brisket, pulled pork, and baby back ribs is excellent.
The meat has a subtle smoke flavor and maintains a moist texture well.

Side menus are also carefully prepared: high quality, including mac and cheese, coleslaw, pickles, and corn bread.

Various sauce choices (smoky/spicy, etc.) → You can combine them to your taste.

🔸 Atmosphere & Space

The exterior is discreetly hidden, giving the feel of a ‘hidden restaurant’.

The interior is dark and wood-toned, with a slight factory feel + a local American bar feel.

It's overall casual but has a macho feel, so it's good to visit with friends.

The smell of grilling meat and smoke also completes the store atmosphere.

🔸 Price & Configuration

Approximately 25,000~35,000 won per person based on set menu.

The amount of meat is generous so it feels like 1.5 servings.

Goes well with craft beer or whiskey.

🔸 Visiting Tips

There may be a wait during evening hours → Reservation recommended

It may close early if the meat runs out, so visiting late at night is not recommended.

It was early in the morning, and the streets and the store were deserted, perhaps because of the coronavirus, so the female salesperson was cleaning the glass door of the store and greeted me as I entered.

Since I stopped by without any specific information, I asked if there was a particularly popular flavor. He said it all depends on my taste and told me to try samples and that I could taste as many as I wanted.

I wanted to try them all, but I wanted to taste Earl Gray, Lemon Cookie, Mexican Vanilla, Pistachio, and even though they weren't on display, I asked for triple berry and chocolate mint, and when I tasted them, I guess I liked the classic taste, so they were all good, but I liked Mexican vanilla and pistachio, triple berry had a nice freshness of berry, and chocolate mint had a minty mint flavor, but Mexican vanilla was the best. I asked for the Mexican Vanilla in a cone because cups and cones are the same price.

Perhaps it was because it was early in the morning and she was free, or maybe it was because the clerk didn't seem to have been working long, but the friendly female clerk put it in a cone and, unlike the usual Baskin Robbins, carefully weighed it and handed it over to me.

When I left the store and tasted it, I liked the yellowish scent of Mexican vanilla. It felt better than Baskin Robbins, but it didn't have the American feel or flavor like the Korean brand Yeoseonji Galwol-dong Sticky Ricky. It was relatively mild, so it wasn't a wow-worthy taste, so I felt it was okay just for the taste, but it was still better than Baskin Robbins, and I liked the friendly service of the clerk and the cleanly managed store. In fact, as I passed by the front of the store, I saw that all 2 tables were occupied.

As I couldn't help but think about what to do, I had lunch at Seongbuk-dong Pork Ribs Restaurant last time and wanted to try it for dessert, but since it opened in the late afternoon, I decided to stop by Hotteokdang, which I couldn't try because it wasn't open yet for lunch.

It was close, so I arrived quickly and there were a few customers in front of the store. After looking at the menu, I ordered one of the most basic dishes, honey hotteok.

Next to the pan where the hotteoks are fried, there are pre-fried hotteoks, but rather than putting the filling in the dough and frying it like most hotteok restaurants, they instead fry hotteoks that have already been made at the factory and fry them in oil when they are ordered, which was a bit disappointing.

It was no different from the Peacock Hotteok that I like and sell at E-Mart, which is also in the kitchen at my house.

No, the Peacock hotteok is so good that I wonder if there is any reason to eat it at a hotteok restaurant unless it is especially delicious.

Anyway, I waited a little while to taste it, and Sajam cut four pieces with scissors in the east, west, north, south, and north directions and handed it to me in a paper cup that opened up so that the hotteok could easily fit in. He told me to eat it carefully because it was very hot inside.

While blowing to avoid getting burned, I bit into the flour bread part with my teeth, and the dough felt somewhat like bread rather than being chewy and light. It was less moist and oily, but I was disappointed because it felt relatively dry and crumbly and had a factory-shaped feel.

After biting into a bit of the bread, I could see the honey filling inside, but there was a relatively generous amount of crushed peanuts, and the taste and cinnamon scent were somewhat good, so it wasn't bad. However, it was not a cow that felt special.

Overall, I stopped by because the hotteok seems to be famous, and it is good that the honey filling with plenty of ground peanuts is pre-made at the factory, more generous and even than the common instant hotteok, but the shape is too even and the dough feels a bit dry and crumbly rather than lightly chewy, so it feels unfamiliar. Personally, I think other jams would also suit it. On the other hand, I already thought that the bread at this place would be delicious, but I expected the drinks to taste like an ordinary cafe or coffee shop, but I felt that the visual and taste provided definitely matched Sandwich. It's refreshingly delicious. The baguette bread is chewy, so it's fun to tear it with incisors... Looking at other photos, it looks like they also sell soups, but it would be delicious to eat with cream of mushroom soup or Clem chowder soup.
